ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The Bode plot of a transfer function \( G(s) \) is shown in the image. The gain \( 20 \log |G(j\omega)| \) is 32 dB and -8 dB at 1 rad/s and 10 rad/s respectively, and the phase is negative for all \( \omega \). Determine \( G(s) \).
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the Bode magnitude-frequency plot in the figure is a straight line descending to the right; at \(\omega=1\,\text{rad/s}\), the gain is marked as approximately \(32\,\text{dB}\), and at \(\omega=10\,\text{rad/s}\), the corresponding dashed line marks approximately \(-8\,\text{dB}\). Therefore, within one decade from 1 to 10 rad/s, the magnitude drops from 32 dB to -8 dB. Then reason: the slope is \((-8-32)/(\log_{10}10-\log_{10}1)=-40\,\text{dB/decade}\). A Bode magnitude-frequency slope of \(-40\,\text{dB/decade}\) indicates that there are two integrating elements, so set \(G(s)=K/s^2\). When \(\omega=1\), \(|G(j1)|=|K/(j1)^2|=K\), so \(20\log_{10}K=32\), obtaining \(K=10^{32/20}\approx39.8\). The problem states that the phase is negative for all \(\omega\); \(K/s^2\) with a positive coefficient corresponds to phase \(-180^\circ\), consistent with the condition. Therefore \(G(s)=39.8/s^2\).
